title: Dasakam 48 — Naḷakūbara-Maṇigrīvayoḥ śāpamōkṣam
description: Damodara sees the twin Arjuna trees; Kubera’s sons are transformed, released by Krishna, and return to devotion while Vraja brings the unharmed child home.
translation_note: No sourced English verse translation is present in the supplied D048 bundle; translation_en is intentionally empty. Supplied photo captions remain editorial commentary, not verse translation.

stanzas.sanskrit:
मुदा सुरौघैस्त्वमुदारसम्मदै-
-रुदीर्य दामोदर इत्यभिष्टुतः ।
मृदूदरः स्वैरमुलूखले लग-
-न्नदूरतो द्वौ ककुभावुदैक्षथाः ॥ ४८-१ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
mudā suraughaistvamudārasammadai-
-rudīrya dāmōdara ityabhiṣṭutaḥ |
mr̥dūdaraḥ svairamulūkhalē laga-
-nadūratō dvau kakubhāvudaikṣathāḥ || 48-1 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Yashoda tied Krishna to the mortar and went to look after her house hold chores. Devas and great sages praised Bhagwan and called him Damodara in excitement. Krishna stayed tied by a hard rope on his soft stomach and watched the two trees in front of his house.

stanzas.sanskrit:
कुबेरसूनुर्नलकूबराभिधः
परो मणिग्रीव इति प्रथां गतः ।
महेशसेवाधिगतश्रियोन्मदौ
चिरं किल त्वद्विमुखावखेलताम् ॥ ४८-२ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kubērasūnurnalakūbarābhidhaḥ
parō maṇigrīva iti prathāṁ gataḥ |
mahēśasēvādhigataśriyōnmadau
ciraṁ kila tvadvimukhāvakhēlatām || 48-2 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Kubera had two sons, Nalakubura and Manigriva. They were devoted to Lord Shiva and were blessed with lot of wealth. This made them proud and started to indulge in undesirable activities.

stanzas.sanskrit:
सुरापगायां किल तौ मदोत्कटौ
सुरापगायाद्बहुयौवतावृतौ ।
विवाससौ केलिपरौ स नारदो
भवत्पदैकप्रवणो निरैक्षत ॥ ४८-३ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
surāpagāyāṁ kila tau madōtkaṭau
surāpagāyadbahuyauvatāvr̥tau |
vivāsasau kēliparau sa nāradō
bhavatpadaikapravaṇō niraikṣata || 48-3 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Narada who was devoted to Lord Hari, once spotted them singing and sporting in Ganges, taking bath without dress, surrounded by ladies in an intoxicated state.

stanzas.sanskrit:
भिया प्रियालोकमुपात्तवाससं
पुरो निरीक्ष्यापि मदान्धचेतसौ ।
इमौ भवद्भक्त्युपशान्तिसिद्धये
मुनिर्जगौ शान्तिमृते कुतः सुखम् ॥ ४८-४ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhiyā priyālōkamupāttavāsasaṁ
purō nirīkṣyāpi madāndhacētāsau |
imau bhavadbhaktyupaśāntisiddhayē
munirjagau śāntimr̥tē kutaḥ sukham || 48-4 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Seeing Narada, the women hurriedly put on their clothes. Narada cursed the duo to become devoted to Bhagwan and attain peace. Without peace, there is no way anyone can achieve happiness.

transcription_note.note: The earlier project Roman string madāndhacētāsau lengthened the a after t. Stotra Nidhi’s source Roman line is madāndhacetasau and its Devanagari reads मदान्धचेतसौ; the project extended-vowel spelling is madāndhacētasau. This correction changes no Sanskrit or translation.

stanzas.sanskrit:
युवामवाप्तौ ककुभात्मतां चिरं
हरिं निरीक्ष्याथ पदं स्वमाप्नुतम् ।
इतीरितौ तौ भवदीक्षणस्पृहां
गतौ व्रजान्ते ककुभौ बभूवतुः ॥ ४८-५ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
yuvāmavāptau kakubhātmatāṁ ciraṁ
hariṁ nirīkṣyātha padaṁ svamāpnutam |
itīritau tau bhavadīkṣaṇaspr̥hāṁ
gatau vrajāntē kakubhau babhūvatuḥ || 48-5 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Sage cursed both to become trees for a very long time and wait to get the darshan of Bhagwan to achieve peace and their original form. Immediately Nalakubura and Manigriva became Kakuba or Arjuna trees and waited to have darshan of Bhagwan near Gokulam.

stanzas.sanskrit:
अतन्द्रमिन्द्रद्रुयुगं तथाविधं
समेयुषा मन्थरगामिना त्वया ।
तिरायितोलूखलरोधनिर्धुतौ
चिराय जीर्णौ परिपातितौ तरू ॥ ४८-६ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
atandramindradruyugaṁ tathāvidhaṁ
samēyuṣā mantharagāminā tvayā |
tirāyitōlūkhalarōdhanirdhutau
cirāya jīrṇau paripātitau tarū || 48-6 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna pulled the mortar along and started to move towards the trees in a slow paced manner. The mortar was made horizontal by krishna so he can roll it along and walked between the trees.

stanzas.sanskrit:
अभाजि शाखिद्वितयं यदा त्वया
तदैव तद्गर्भतलान्निरेयुषा ।
महात्विषा यक्षयुगेन तत्क्षणा-
-दभाजि गोविन्द भवानपि स्तवैः ॥ ४८-७ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
abhāji śākhidvitayaṁ yadā tvayā
tadaiva tadgarbhatalānnirēyuṣā |
mahātviṣā yakṣayugēna tatkṣaṇā-
dabhāji gōvinda bhavānapi stavaiḥ || 48-7 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: The mortar hit the old decayed trees and both fell down. Two radiant yakshas, Nalakubura and Manigriva emerged from the roots of the felled trees and immediately sang hymns in praise of Bhagwan and worshipped him.

stanzas.sanskrit:
इहान्यभक्तोऽपि समेष्यति क्रमात्
भवन्तमेतौ खलु रुद्रसेवकौ ।
मुनिप्रसादाद्भवदङ्घ्रिमागतौ
गतौ वृणानौ खलु भक्तिमुत्तमाम् ॥ ४८-८ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ihānyabhaktō:’pi samēṣyati kramāt
bhavantamētau khalu rudrasēvakau |
muniprasādādbhavadaṅghrimāgatau
gatau vr̥ṇānau khalu bhaktimuttamām || 48-8 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: By the mercy of sage Narada, here, the two sons of Kuberan reached Bhagwam’s  feet and were blessed with the boon of highest devotion to Bhagwan always and went away.

stanzas.sanskrit:
ततस्तरूद्दारणदारुणारव-
-प्रकम्पिसम्पातिनि गोपमण्डले ।
विलज्जितत्वज्जननीमुखेक्षिणा
व्यमोक्षि नन्देन भवान्विमोक्षदः ॥ ४८-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tatastarūddāraṇadāruṇārava-
-prakampisampātini gōpamaṇḍalē |
vilajjitatvajjananīmukhēkṣiṇā
vyamōkṣi nandēna bhavānvimōkṣadaḥ || 48-9 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: The gopas rushed to the place after hearing the frightening sound of falling trees. Nandagopan looked at Yashoda meaningfully and she felt ashamed of her act. He then released Krishna from the mortar, who releases everyone in this world from the bonds of samsara and maya.

stanzas.sanskrit:
महीरुहोर्मध्यगतो बतार्भको
हरेः प्रभावादपरिक्षतोऽधुना ।
इति ब्रुवाणैर्गमितो गृहं भवान्
मरुत्पुराधीश्वर पाहि मां गदात् ॥ ४८-१० ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
mahīruhōrmadhyagatō batārbhakō
harēḥ prabhāvādaparikṣatō:’dhunā |
iti bruvāṇairgamitō gr̥haṁ bhavān
marutpurādhīśvara pāhi māṁ gadāt || 48-10 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
It is Bhagwan’s mercy that the child was protected even though he was caught between the falling trees. Saying this, Nandagopan and gopas went home with Krishna.
Bhattathiri requests Lord Guruvayoorappan to free him from ailments.
